classification.assetImpact: No asset theft or permanent loss. Temporary denial of service on principal: while phUSD mint authorization is revoked, PhlimboV3._claimRewards:863 (un-banked phUSD.mint) reverts, which reverts every stake/withdraw/claim for every staker. Principal remains fully recoverable — owner re-grants the mint role or uses emergencyTransfer.
attackPath: 1. Owner/operator calls phUSD.revokeAllMintPrivileges() or setMinter(PhlimboV3,false) — typically to contain an UNRELATED minter incident on the shared ecosystem token.
2. PhlimboV3._claimRewards:863 phUSD.mint(beneficiary,...) is not _tryTransfer+bank wrapped (unlike the stable :876 and promo :902 legs).
3. Every staker's stake/withdraw/claim reverts because the reward-claim leg reverts inline — principal is frozen.
4. Recovery: owner re-grants mint authorization (unfreezes) or emergencyTransfer principal out-of-band.
classification.likelihood: low — requires a privileged owner action; there is NO unprivileged/permissionless trigger. The freeze is a non-obvious side effect of a global kill-switch, hence a footgun, but it cannot be induced by an external attacker.
classification.assumptions: phUSD is the protocol's own first-party mintable token; revokeAllMintPrivileges() is its global ecosystem kill-switch; owner is non-malicious.
classification.externalRequirements: A privileged phUSD authorization revocation must occur. No blocklist, no third-party token weirdness, no attacker action.

classifiedFindings.severityRationale: Caps at Low, and does NOT inherit its Medium parent. The parent V3-M-05 was Medium precisely because its trigger was UNprivileged (a USDC-blocklist path any environment could hit). The residual on the phUSD leg has a fundamentally weaker vector: the only trigger is an owner-privileged authorization revocation, and the resulting freeze is fully owner-reversible with no asset loss. Under C4, a DoS that requires a privileged action AND is recoverable by that same privilege is QA/Low. It stays IN SCOPE (not suppressed) as a Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun — a competent non-malicious operator pulling the shared-token kill-switch would be surprised that it freezes V3 principal — and carries safe-config guidance: bank/try-wrap the phUSD mint leg symmetric with the stable/promo legs so an authorization revert cannot brick principal. Not the FoT/weird-token known-invalid.
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Wrap the phUSD.mint leg at :863 in the same _tryTransfer+bank pattern as the stable (:876) and promo (:902) legs, so a mint-authorization revert defers the reward rather than reverting the whole stake/withdraw/claim path.

classification.assetImpact: PhlimboV3-side unclaimable stable/promo banked with MigratorV2V3 as beneficiary is stranded from the migrator's perspective — MigratorV2V3 exposes no function that calls PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimableStable/Promo (no forwarder / self-pull). Value is NOT lost to the protocol: owner can sweep it via emergencyTransfer out-of-band.
attackPath: 1. Migrator processes a straggler pass and accrues pending stable/promo on the PhlimboV3 side, banked to unclaimable*Of[migrator].
2. The migrator's own address is blocklisted mid-pass (exotic precondition) so the direct transfer path fails and value falls into the PhlimboV3-side unclaimable bank.
3. MigratorV2V3 has no function that pulls that bank -> value is unreachable via the migrator.
classification.likelihood: very low — requires the migrator's own address to be blocklisted at the exact moment it holds accrued pending; recoverable by owner.
classification.assumptions: Blocklisting token; owner non-malicious and available to run emergencyTransfer.
classification.externalRequirements: Third-party token must blocklist the migrator's address mid-straggler-pass with accrued pending.

classifiedFindings.severityRationale: Low/informational. No asset theft and no permanent loss — the stranded bank is fully owner-recoverable via emergencyTransfer, and the trigger is an exotic precondition (self-blocklist mid-pass with accrued pending). Availability impact is confined to one migrator identity's residual bank, not protocol function, so it does not reach Medium. Kept in scope (recall beats report-tidiness) as a design/operational footgun: the migrator lacks a self-pull forwarder for its PhlimboV3-side unclaimable bank. Distinct from V3-L-08, V3-F-01, V3-Q-01 (different banks/root-causes).
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Add a forwarder on MigratorV2V3 that calls PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimableStable/Promo for itself, so the migrator can recover its own PhlimboV3-side bank without owner intervention.
